#929 (issue-929), the sharing wave, re-pinned ONCE over the #916 baseline. A share stopped being a second membership plane and became a REPLICA SUBSCRIPTION. What moved in packages/vault/src/schema:
(1) THE COMMONS RAIL LEFT. `schema/share-commons.ts` and `schema/commons-resilience.ts` are deleted, taking fourteen tables with them: share_circle_grant, share_commons_member_state, _op, _replay, _receipt, _cursor, _lineage, _retained, _intent, _invitation, _verified, _supersession, _device_reach and _steward_contact. None of them held a row a bundle would lose: every SHARED row is an ordinary entity row the canonical walk already carries, and the rest was CONTROL state — an op log, its chain and checkpoints, a roster, a steward's contact card — for a plane that no longer exists. `migrateCommonsToSubscriptions` (share/subscription-migration.ts, run once per vault on mount) turns each live circle grant into standing `share_authority` answers with `share_fulfillment` delivery rows and THEN drops the tables, so a pre-#929 file loses nothing it could still use and a fresh file never has them.
(2) TWO TABLES ENTERED, both in the canonical walk. `share_subscription` (shape_id, audience_vault_id) is the audience seat's own record of what it holds and how far its cursor has come; `share_subscription_lineage` (shape_id, target_type, target_id) is the many-to-many claim of WHICH local rows arrived under WHICH shape, carrying `origin_item_id` and `origin_row_version`. The lineage is the load-bearing half of export completeness here: a bundle that dropped it would restore a seat that can no longer remove what a revocation ends, and two overlapping grants over one row could not be told apart. Neither table is LOCAL, and `exportVault`'s SELECT * carries both with no adapter.
(3) share_party_vault_binding MOVED MODULES, not shape. Its DDL and the `social_circle_member.capability` column left the deleted commons module for `schema/party-vault-binding.ts`, byte-identical, still registered, still exported.
(4) replica_intent GAINED `waiting_on` and `answered_versions` (schema/replica.ts), so a parked member write can say WHO it waits on and which origin row versions its answer stands for. `replica_*` is LOCAL by registration, so neither column enters a bundle — correct, because both are facts about this device's queue rather than about the vault's data.
(5) REGISTRY EDITS, no DDL: entity-catalog.ts, entity-refs.ts, party-pointers.ts and local-tables.ts drop the commons entries and gain the two subscription ones; `schema/entity.ts`'s generated trigger no longer names share_circle_grant; migrate.test.ts and ontology-rules.test.ts follow. No other table entered or left the walk, and no sealed cell changed class.
EXPORT COMPLETENESS RE-AUDITED in packages/vault/src/gateway/portable-export.ts, whose #929 note states the lineage rule above next to the bands it belongs with.
